nodes.label: DNA Methylation
nodes.description: DNA methylation is one of the three best-studied epigenetic mechanisms, involving addition of methyl groups to cytosines at CpG dinucleotides.

nodes.label: Epigenetics
nodes.description: DNA methylation is one of the three best-studied epigenetic mechanisms, involving addition of methyl groups to cytosines at CpG dinucleotides.

nodes.label: Histone Modification
nodes.description: Histone modification — covalent marks on histone tails including acetylation, methylation, phosphorylation, ubiquitination — is a core epigenetic mechanism.

nodes.label: Non-Coding RNA
nodes.description: Non-coding RNAs such as MicroRNA and piRNAs regulate gene expression transcriptionally and post-transcriptionally as an epigenetic mechanism.

nodes.label: DNA Methyltransferase
nodes.description: The process of DNA methylation is catalyzed by a family of enzymes called DNA Methyltransferases (DNMTs).

nodes.label: DNMT1
nodes.description: DNMT1 is the primary enzyme responsible for maintaining DNA methylation patterns during DNA Replication, copying the methylation pattern of the parental strand onto the daughter strand.

nodes.label: UHRF1
nodes.description: During S Phase, DNMT1 is recruited to replication foci through its interaction with UHRF1, which recognizes hemi-methylated CpG sites via its SRA domain.

nodes.label: SAM
nodes.description: DNMT1 transfers a methyl group from S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) to the C5 position of cytosine on the nascent strand.

nodes.label: DNMT3a
nodes.description: DNMT3a is a de novo methyltransferase responsible for establishing new DNA methylation patterns at previously unmethylated DNA.

nodes.label: DNMT3b
nodes.description: DNMT3a forms complexes with its paralog DNMT3b and with the accessory protein DNMT3L to deposit methylation at targeted loci.

nodes.label: Gene Bodies
nodes.description: DNMT3a exhibits a preference for gene bodies and intergenic regions, in contrast to DNMT3b which favors repetitive elements.

nodes.label: Hematopoiesis
nodes.description: DNMT3a remains crucial for hematopoiesis — especially hematopoietic stem cell differentiation and self-renewal.

nodes.label: Clonal Hematopoiesis
nodes.description: Somatic mutations in DNMT3A are among the most common drivers of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP).

nodes.label: Acute Myeloid Leukemia
nodes.description: Recurrent DNMT3A mutations (notably R882H) are found in ~20% of acute myeloid leukemia (AML) cases.

nodes.label: Pericentromeric Satellite Repeats
nodes.description: DNMT3b exhibits a strong preference for pericentromeric satellite repeats and other repetitive DNA, depositing methylation essential for heterochromatin formation.

nodes.label: ICF Syndrome
nodes.description: Mutations in the DNMT3B gene are the cause of ICF Syndrome (Immunodeficiency, Centromere instability, and Facial anomalies).

nodes.label: Gene Silencing
nodes.description: High levels of methylation in promoter regions, often concentrated in CpG Islands, are strongly associated with gene silencing.

nodes.label: Chromatin Remodeling
nodes.description: Methylated DNA is recognized by MBD proteins that recruit chromatin remodeling factors and histone deacetylases, leading to condensed transcriptionally inactive chromatin.

nodes.label: Epigenetic Clock
nodes.description: Epigenetic clocks are built from DNA methylation measurements at defined CpG sites whose methylation changes predictably with age.

nodes.label: Transposable Elements
nodes.description: DNA methylation helps repress potentially harmful repetitive elements and retrotransposons within the genome.

nodes.label: Histone Acetyltransferase
nodes.description: Histone Acetyltransferase (HAT) transfers an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to specific lysine residues on histone tails, a key component of epigenetic regulation.

nodes.label: Histone Acetylation
nodes.description: Histone Acetyltransferase (HAT) transfers an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to specific lysine residues on histone tails, a key component of epigenetic regulation.

nodes.label: Histone Deacetylase
nodes.description: HATs act in dynamic opposition to HDACs; signal-dependent recruitment of HATs couples extracellular cues to gene activation.

nodes.label: Euchromatin
nodes.description: Acetylation neutralizes the positive charge of histone tails, transitioning chromatin from condensed to open, transcriptionally active euchromatin.

nodes.label: Acetyl-CoA
nodes.description: HATs transfer an acetyl group from acetyl-CoA to specific lysine residues on histone tails.

nodes.label: Histone Deacetylation
nodes.description: HDACs remove acetyl groups from ε-N-acetyl-lysine residues on histones, allowing chromatin to wrap DNA more tightly and generally repressing transcription.

nodes.label: Heterochromatin
nodes.description: By removing acetyl groups, HDACs restore positive charge of lysine side chains, strengthening interaction with DNA and leading to more condensed heterochromatin.

nodes.label: Sirtuins
nodes.description: Class III HDACs are the Sirtuins (SIRT1–7), NAD+-dependent deacetylases that link metabolic state to chromatin regulation.

nodes.label: Deacetylases
nodes.description: Sirtuins are NAD+-dependent deacetylases that link metabolic state to chromatin regulation and are strongly implicated in aging and longevity.

nodes.label: Yeast
nodes.description: Overexpression of Sir2 extends lifespan in yeast by preventing the formation of toxic rDNA circles.

nodes.label: H4K16
nodes.description: Sir2/SIRT1 is an H4K16 deacetylase required for silencing and chromatin compaction at mating type loci, rDNA, and telomeres.

nodes.label: LINE-1
nodes.description: SIRT6 is enriched at LINE-1 5'UTR loci and mono-ADP ribosylates KAP1, promoting heterochromatinization of L1 elements.

nodes.label: HAT
nodes.description: HAT is the common abbreviation for Histone Acetyltransferase.

nodes.label: HDAC
nodes.description: HDAC stands for Histone Deacetylase.

nodes.label: Biological Age
nodes.description: An epigenetic clock is a statistical estimator of biological age built from DNA methylation measurements at a defined set of CpG sites.

nodes.label: DNAmGrimAge
nodes.description: DNAmGrimAge is a second-generation epigenetic clock trained to predict morbidity, mortality, and physiological decline rather than time.

nodes.label: Partial Reprogramming
nodes.description: Partial cellular reprogramming has shown measurable epigenetic clock reversal, motivating use of clocks as endpoints in rejuvenation trials.

nodes.label: Epigenetic Drift
nodes.description: The best-characterized signature of epigenetic drift is global hypomethylation of repetitive elements and gene bodies coupled with site-specific hypermethylation of gene promoters.

nodes.label: Global Hypomethylation
nodes.description: The best-characterized signature of epigenetic drift is global hypomethylation of repetitive elements and gene bodies coupled with site-specific hypermethylation of gene promoters.

nodes.label: Yamanaka Factors
nodes.description: The Yamanaka Factors (OSKM: Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) are used to induce pluripotency in differentiated Somatic Cells.

nodes.label: Somatic Cells
nodes.description: The Yamanaka Factors (OSKM: Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) are used to induce pluripotency in differentiated Somatic Cells.

nodes.label: Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
nodes.description: The four Yamanaka Factors revert fibroblasts to an embryonic-stem-cell-like state, generating iPSCs.

nodes.label: Klf4
nodes.description: The Yamanaka Factors comprise Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc.

nodes.label: c-Myc
nodes.description: The Yamanaka Factors comprise Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, and c-Myc.

nodes.label: OSKM
nodes.description: The Yamanaka Factors are also known as the OSKM cassette (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc).

nodes.label: Pluripotency
nodes.description: Oct4 is a definitive marker and master regulator of pluripotency, essential for self-renewal of undifferentiated ES cells and iPSCs.

nodes.label: Mesenchymal-to-Epithelial Transition
nodes.description: During Cellular Reprogramming, Oct4 initiates the mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition and resets the epigenome.

nodes.label: H3K9me3
nodes.description: During reprogramming, H3K9me3/H3K27me3 repressive marks are erased at Oct4 target loci.

nodes.label: Neural Stem Cell
nodes.description: Sox2 maintains Neural Stem Cell identity in the adult SVZ/SGZ and is required for tissue homeostasis in multiple epithelia.

nodes.label: Snail
nodes.description: Klf4 opposes the EMT drivers Snail and Slug, sitting at the polarity between epithelial identity and mesenchymal dispersal.

nodes.label: Slug
nodes.description: Klf4 opposes the EMT drivers Snail and Slug during reprogramming.

nodes.label: Cellular Reprogramming
nodes.description: Cellular Reprogramming is fundamentally an epigenetic remodeling process that erases somatic memory and installs a new identity.

nodes.label: Epigenetic Remodeling
nodes.description: Cellular Reprogramming is fundamentally an epigenetic remodeling process that erases somatic memory and installs a new identity.

nodes.label: Teratoma
nodes.description: Partial reprogramming contrasts with full reprogramming to iPSCs, which risks teratoma formation.

nodes.label: Rejuvenation
nodes.description: The dominant experimental strategy for rejuvenation is Cellular Reprogramming with the Yamanaka Factors (OSKM).

nodes.label: Quiescence
nodes.description: Quiescence is a state of reversible proliferative arrest in which cells exit the Cell Cycle but retain the capacity to re-enter upon appropriate stimuli.

nodes.label: Cell Cycle Arrest
nodes.description: Quiescence is a state of reversible proliferative arrest in which cells exit the Cell Cycle but retain the capacity to re-enter upon appropriate stimuli.

nodes.label: Retinoblastoma Protein
nodes.description: Quiescence is enforced at the Restriction Point by the Retinoblastoma Protein (pRb), which sequesters E2F transcription factors and blocks S-phase genes.

nodes.label: Hematopoietic Stem Cell
nodes.description: Adult stem cells such as Hematopoietic Stem Cells spend most of their lives in quiescence to protect the genome and preserve self-renewal.

nodes.label: RB1
nodes.description: RB1 (product of the Retinoblastoma gene) sequesters E2F transcription factors and blocks S-phase genes to enforce quiescence.

nodes.label: DNA Damage Response
nodes.description: Senescence in adult tissues can be triggered by a persistent DNA damage response (DDR) induced by various internal and external factors.

nodes.label: cGAS-STING Pathway
nodes.description: Cytoplasmic chromatin fragments detected by cGAS activate the cGAS-STING-NF-κB pathways to induce SASP expression.

nodes.label: Cytoplasmic Chromatin Fragments
nodes.description: Senescent cells release damaged DNA into the cytoplasm forming CCF, which is detected by cGAS, activating STING and NF-κB.

nodes.label: DNA Hypomethylation
nodes.description: Age-related DNA demethylation and heterochromatin decompaction activate LINE-1 retrotransposons, triggering cGAS-STING inflammation.

nodes.label: HERV
nodes.description: HERV RNA undergoes reverse transcription in senescent cells, triggering cGAS/STING-dependent upregulation of SASP factors.

nodes.label: H3K27me3
nodes.description: Depleting or inhibiting EZH2 leads to removal of H3K27me3 from SASP loci, enabling derepression of SASP genes.

nodes.label: EZH2
nodes.description: EZH2 is the histone methyltransferase responsible for H3K27me3; its depletion removes H3K27me3 from SASP loci.

nodes.label: KDM4
nodes.description: KDM4 (JMJD2) is the histone demethylase enzyme targeting H3K9; its expression increases in senescent cells, diminishing H3K9 methylation and enhancing SASP.

nodes.label: SUV39H1
nodes.description: SUV39H1 is a histone methyltransferase that specifically trimethylates H3K9; it decreases in senescent cells.

nodes.label: AP-1
nodes.description: The transcription factor AP-1 acts as a pioneering factor that binds to enhancers associated with SASP genes, initiating opening of closed chromatin.

nodes.label: H3K27ac
nodes.description: BRD4 is an epigenetic reader recognizing H3K27ac at senescence-activated super-enhancers, facilitating SASP gene expression.

nodes.label: HDAC4
nodes.description: HDAC4 is recruited to H3K27ac loci to monitor the acetylation status of H3K27 at AP-1 regulated super-enhancers.

nodes.label: Senescence-Associated Heterochromatin Foci
nodes.description: SAHFs are characterized by increased HP1, H3K9me3 marks, macroH2A and HMGA protein binding.

nodes.label: macroH2A
nodes.description: macroH2A is abundant in SAHF where it promotes transcriptional silencing.

nodes.label: H3.3
nodes.description: In senescent cells, H3.3 accumulates and progressively replaces canonical H3.1 and H3.2, and both H3.3 and its cleaved product H3.3cs1 trigger senescence when ectopically expressed.

nodes.label: H2A.J
nodes.description: H2A.J is enriched in SASP promoters, facilitating changes in chromatin accessibility that induce SASP expression.

nodes.label: γ-H2A.X
nodes.description: γ-H2A.X serves as a beacon to recruit DNA repair proteins at the sites of double-stranded DNA breaks.

nodes.label: DNA Repair
nodes.description: γ-H2A.X serves as a beacon to recruit DNA repair proteins at the sites of double-stranded DNA breaks.

nodes.label: Nucleosome Remodeling
nodes.description: During yeast aging, nucleosome occupancy decreases by up to 50% across the genome and half of core histone proteins are lost.

nodes.label: SAHF
nodes.description: SAHF disruption correlates with reduced SASP expression, though whether SAHF is necessary for SASP remains unresolved.

nodes.label: rDNA
nodes.description: Sirtuins stabilize human rDNA by recruiting DNMT1, preventing cellular senescence — essentially the same function as yeast Sir2.

nodes.label: Disease Modeling
nodes.description: iPSCs have transformed Disease Modeling for genetic disorders by generating isogenic neuronal models from patient fibroblasts.

nodes.label: Shinya Yamanaka
nodes.description: iPSC technology was pioneered by Shinya Yamanaka and colleagues in 2006, who demonstrated that four factors could revert fibroblasts to pluripotency.

nodes.label: Epigenetic Modifiers

nodes.label: Decitabine

nodes.label: Sodium Valproate

nodes.label: Trichostatin A

nodes.label: SIRT2 overactivity
nodes.description: Direct activation of SIRT2 is rarely sought because overactivity is associated with neurotoxicity in neurodegeneration contexts.

nodes.label: SIRT2 inhibitors (AGK2, AK-7, SirReal2)
nodes.description: SIRT2 inhibitors are investigated for neurodegenerative diseases where blocking SIRT2 rescues microtubule stability and protects neurons from aggregation toxicity.

nodes.label: Parkinson's and Huntington's disease
nodes.description: SIRT2 inhibitors are investigated for neurodegenerative diseases where blocking SIRT2 rescues microtubule stability and protects neurons from aggregation toxicity.

nodes.label: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide)
nodes.description: NMN and NR serve as universal indirect pan-sirtuin activators by raising cellular NAD+ levels, the obligate co-substrate for all sirtuins.

nodes.label: Universal indirect pan-sirtuin activator
nodes.description: NMN and NR serve as universal indirect pan-sirtuin activators by raising cellular NAD+ levels, the obligate co-substrate for all sirtuins.

nodes.label: NR (Nicotinamide Riboside)
nodes.description: NMN and NR serve as universal indirect pan-sirtuin activators by raising cellular NAD+ levels.

nodes.label: H3K18
nodes.description: SIRT7 is highly localized to the nucleolus and deacetylates histone H3K18 to regulate ribosome biogenesis.

nodes.label: NFKB
nodes.description: SIRT1 has anti-inflammatory effects mediated by the deacetylation and inactivation of the p65 subunit of NF-κB, specifically at Ac-Lys310.

nodes.label: NF-κB signaling pathway
nodes.description: SIRT1 inhibits the transcriptional activity of NF-κB via deacetylation of the p65 (RelA) subunit at Ac-Lys310.

nodes.label: Histone H3K9
nodes.description: SIRT6 attenuated NF-κB expression by deacetylating histone H3K9 in the promoters of NF-κB target genes, hence decreasing inflammation.

nodes.label: NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses
nodes.description: SIRT6 overexpression suppressed NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses in OA development.

nodes.label: SIRT7-kidney-specific knockout
nodes.description: SIRT7-kidney-specific KO mice exhibited diminished inflammation with a reduction in the level of multiple inflammatory factors such as TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-6, and suppression of nuclear NF-κB p65 accumulation.

nodes.label: spliced X-box binding protein 1
nodes.description: activation of a pathway involving SIRT1 and multipotent mesenchymal stromal/stem cell-mediated AMPKα in macrophages, resulting in deacetylation of spliced X-boxbinding protein 1 and subsequent inhibition of the NLRP3 inflammasome.

nodes.label: miR-217
nodes.description: microRNAs (miRNAs) can negatively regulate inflammation by repressing SIRT1. Downregulation of miRNAs such as miR-217 and miR-543 mitigated the inflammatory response.

nodes.label: miR-543
nodes.description: Downregulation of miRNAs such as miR-217 and miR-543 mitigated the inflammatory response by regulating the SIRT1/AMPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.

nodes.label: miR-378
nodes.description: miR-378 reduced SIRT1 activity and facilitated the inflammatory pathway involving NF-κB-TNFα by targeting 5'-AMPK subunit gamma-2.

nodes.label: MCPIP1
nodes.description: the RNase monocyte chemoattractant protein-induced protein 1 alleviated inflammatory responses by promoting the expression of SIRT1 mediated via miR-9.

nodes.label: p53/miR-22 axis
nodes.description: SIRT1 targets the p53/miR-22 axis to suppress inflammation, cyclooxygenase (COX)-2 and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) expression.

nodes.label: PTP1B
nodes.description: SIRT1 increases insulin sensitivity and lowers blood sugar by downregulating protein tyrosine phosphatase 1B, a key negative regulatory protein in the insulin signal transduction pathway.

nodes.label: CREB
nodes.description: Qiang et al. found that SIRT1-dependent cAMP Response Element Binding protein (Creb) deacetylation regulates lipid metabolism.

nodes.label: HNF4α
nodes.description: SIRT2 prevents liver steatosis and lipid metabolic disorders by deacetylation of hepatocyte nuclear factor 4α.

nodes.label: AMPK/PGC-1α pathway
nodes.description: SIRT3 affected mitochondrial metabolic reprogramming by activating the AMPK/peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ coactivator-1α (PGC-1α) pathway.

nodes.label: Nrf2 signaling
nodes.description: The overexpression of SIRT6 in the brain through in vivo gene transfer enhanced Nrf2 signaling and reduced oxidative stress.

nodes.label: JAK2/STAT3 pathway
nodes.description: SIRT6 inhibits the Janus kinase 2/STAT3 pathway, thereby suppressing the growth of GC.

nodes.label: Cervical cancer progression
nodes.description: the expression of SIRT2 is decreased in CC tissue compared with paired adjacent tissue... which predicts favorable survival.

nodes.label: ACC1
nodes.description: Moreover, SIRT3 contributes to the reprogramming of fatty acid synthesis by upregulating acetyl-coA carboxylase 1 to promote de novo lipogenesis by SIRT3 deacetylation, thereby promoting the invasion and metastasis of CC cells.

nodes.label: LC3
nodes.description: SIRT1 promotes autophagy and proliferation of EC cells by reducing acetylation of LC3.

nodes.label: IGF-Akt signaling
nodes.description: SIRT6 blocks IGF-Akt signaling and cardiac hypertrophy development by targeting c-Jun.

nodes.label: NFATc2
nodes.description: SIRT2 binds to and deacetylates the nuclear factor of activated T-cell c2 transcription factor, thereby regulating nuclear factor of activated T-cell c2 transcription activity.

nodes.label: MnSOD activity
nodes.description: SIRT4 overexpression aggravates Ang II-induced cardiac hypertrophy by inhibiting MnSOD activity.

nodes.label: TGF-β/Smad3 pathway
nodes.description: activation of both SIRT1 and SIRT3 by resveratrol attenuates cardiac fibrosis in mice by inhibiting the TGF-β/Smad3 pathway.

nodes.label: Cardiac fibrosis
nodes.description: SIRT4 appears to contribute to cardiac fibrosis, and global SIRT4 KO in mice confers resistance to Ang II infusion by significantly suppressing fibrosis deposition.

nodes.label: SERCA2a
nodes.description: the pharmacological activation of SIRT1 restores SERCA2a activity via deacetylation at K492.

nodes.label: Lox-1-mediated foam cell formation
nodes.description: SIRT1 activation reduces Lox-1-mediated foam cell formation via suppression of the NF-κB signaling pathway.

nodes.label: VSMC proliferation and migration
nodes.description: SIRT7 has been reported to regulate the VSMC proliferation and migration via the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway.

nodes.label: MDL-800
nodes.description: The bis benzenesulfonamide-based prodrug MDL-800 is also reported to be a potent and selective SIRT6 activator with an EC50 value of 10.3 μM.

nodes.label: EX-527 (Selisistat)
nodes.description: EX-527, also called Selisistat, is the first known selective (over SIRT2/3) and cell-permeable SIRT1 (IC50 = 0.098 μM) inhibitor.

nodes.label: SirReal2
nodes.description: SirReal2 is a potent SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.14 μM) with minimal effects on SIRT1 and SIRT3.

nodes.label: Suramin
nodes.description: Suramin, a polyanionic urea derivative, was potent SIRT inhibitor with an IC50 of 297 nM, 1150 nM, and 22 μM for SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT5, respectively.

nodes.label: TGF-β1-induced apoptosis and fibrosis
nodes.description: overexpression of SIRT1 abolished TGF-β1-induced cell apoptosis and fibrosis, and suppressed CTGF expression via stimulation by TGF-β1 in mouse kidneys.

nodes.label: TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation
nodes.description: genetic knockdown and chemical inhibition of SIRT2 attenuated TGF-β1-induced fibroblast activation and mouse double minute 2 protein expression.

nodes.label: pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α
nodes.description: Pyruvate dehydrogenase E1α is hyperacetylated at lysine 385 in tubular epithelial cells after TGFβ1 stimulation and is regulated by SIRT3.

nodes.label: osteogenic transdifferentiation of VSMCs
nodes.description: SIRT6 suppressed the osteogenic transdifferentiation of VSMCs via regulation of runt-related transcription factor 2.

nodes.label: UUO-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis
nodes.description: the SIRT6 activator MDL-800 mitigated UUO-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis.
nodes.norm_label: uuo-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis

nodes.label: SIRT1 (dendritic cells)
nodes.description: SIRT1 knockout in dendritic cells (DCs) restrained the generation of regulatory T cells.

nodes.label: Foxp3+ regulatory T cells differentiation

nodes.label: T helper type 1 cells development
nodes.description: SIRT1 knockout in dendritic cells (DCs) drove T helper 1 cell development, promoting inflammation.

nodes.label: SIRT6 deficiency (macrophages)
nodes.description: SIRT6 deficiency in macrophages resulted in inflammation with increases in acetylation and greater stability of FoxO1.

nodes.label: SIRT6 (pancreatic β cells)
nodes.description: SIRT6 in pancreatic β cells deacetylates FoxO1 to maintain glucose-sensing ability and systemic glucose tolerance.

nodes.label: GLUT2
nodes.description: SIRT6 deacetylated FoxO1 and subsequently increased the expression of glucose-dependent transporter 2 (GLUT2).

nodes.label: Preadipocyte differentiation
nodes.description: SIRT5 inhibited preadipocyte differentiation and lipid deposition by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK pathways.

nodes.label: Autophagosome-lysosome fusion
nodes.description: TFEB plays a critical role in the fusion of autophagosomes and lysosomes.

nodes.label: LDHB
nodes.description: SIRT5-induced deacetylation of lactate dehydrogenase B (LDHB) triggers hyperactivation of autophagy.

nodes.label: SIRT5-mediated deacetylation of LDHB
nodes.description: SIRT5-induced deacetylation of lactate dehydrogenase B (LDHB) triggers hyperactivation of autophagy; a key event in tumorigenesis.

nodes.label: Hyperactivation of autophagy
nodes.description: SIRT5-induced deacetylation of lactate dehydrogenase B (LDHB) triggers hyperactivation of autophagy; a key event in tumorigenesis.

nodes.label: Nkx3.2
nodes.description: SIRT6 induced the expression of GATA5 through inhibition of Nkx3.2 transcription by deacetylating histone H3K9.

nodes.label: GATA5
nodes.description: SIRT6 induced the expression of GATA binding protein 5 (GATA5) to prevent endothelial injury.

nodes.label: Polyphenol stilbene (3,4',5-trihydroxystilbene)
nodes.description: The polyphenol stilbene molecule Resveratrol, also known as (3,4',5-trihydroxystilbene).

nodes.label: Grape skin
nodes.description: This polyphenol stilbene identified in grape skin, is believed to be the main component contributing to the anti-atherosclerotic benefits linked to red wine consumption.

nodes.label: Traditional East Asian medicine (Veratrum formosanum)
nodes.description: This ancient stilbene has long been utilized as a component of Veratrum formosanum in traditional East Asian medicine.

nodes.label: Endothelial cells from lipid damage
nodes.description: It has demonstrated the ability to protect endothelial cells from lipid damage.

nodes.label: Vasodilation via nitric oxide synthesis modulation

nodes.label: Smooth muscle cell proliferation

nodes.label: Coronary relaxation

nodes.label: Ventricular arrhythmias

nodes.label: Glucose metabolism
nodes.description: Resveratrol improves glucose metabolism and reduces LDL while elevating HDL.

nodes.label: Direct antioxidant (weaker than vitamin C)

nodes.label: Anti-neoplastic effects

nodes.label: Angiogenic activity during vascular remodeling

nodes.label: Angiotensin II type 1 receptor expression

nodes.label: TIMP3 (tissue metalloproteinase 3)
nodes.description: SIRT1 has been reported to be a regulator of tissue metalloproteinase 3 (TIMP3), an endogenous enzyme which defends vascular inflammation.

nodes.label: Nuclear SIRT1 (enhanced by resveratrol)

nodes.label: Superoxide dismutase in cardiomyocytes
nodes.description: Nuclear SIRT1 enhanced by resveratrol was found to induce superoxide dismutase, an antioxidant enzyme which suppressed cell death in cardiomyocytes.

nodes.description: Transgenic mouse models engineered for over-expression of SIRT3 were significantly less amenable to stimuli-induced hypertrophy.

nodes.label: SIRT7-deficient mice
nodes.description: SIRT7 deficient mice had myocardium defined by extensive fibrosis and high basal rates of apoptosis, resulting in high levels of cardiomyopathy.

nodes.label: Extensive myocardial fibrosis and cardiomyopathy
nodes.description: SIRT7 deficient mice had myocardium defined by extensive fibrosis and high basal rates of apoptosis, resulting in high levels of cardiomyopathy.

nodes.label: Nrf2 (via Keap1 modification)

nodes.label: Heart failure (via SERCA2a deacetylation)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates SERCA2a at K492, restoring its activity and improving cardiac function in heart failure.

nodes.description: SIRT6 prevents TGF-β1-induced lung myofibroblast differentiation by inactivating TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling.

nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates mitofusin 2 at K655 and K662; loss of SIRT1 causes defective autophagy.

nodes.label: p53 at Lys379
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylating p53 at Lys379 inhibits p53-dependent apoptosis.

nodes.label: AMPK (preadipocyte differentiation)
nodes.description: SIRT5 inhibits preadipocyte differentiation by activating AMPK and repressing MAPK signaling pathways.

nodes.label: SIRT1 (feedback inhibition)
nodes.description: Nicotinamide acts as an endogenous non-competitive feedback inhibitor of sirtuins, binding to a conserved pocket within the catalytic domain.

nodes.label: Nicotinamide to NMN

nodes.label: TGF-beta1

nodes.label: SMAD3
nodes.description: TGF-beta1 binds TβRII, which recruits and phosphorylates TβRI, leading to SMAD2/3 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation.

nodes.label: Pathological fibrosis
nodes.description: TGF-beta1 activates SMAD3-dependent transcription of pro-fibrotic genes (COL1A1, COL3A1, FN1, ACTA2, TIMP1) across multiple organs.

nodes.label: BRCA1

nodes.label: Homologous recombination repair
nodes.description: BRCA1 is recruited to DSBs by the MRN complex, promotes end resection, and facilitates RAD51 loading via PALB2/BRCA2.

nodes.description: Loss of BRCA1 leads to increased autophagy as a compensatory survival mechanism in breast and ovarian cancers.

nodes.label: Compensatory autophagy
nodes.description: Loss of BRCA1 leads to increased autophagy as a compensatory survival mechanism in breast and ovarian cancers.

nodes.label: BRCA1 mutation
nodes.description: BRCA1-deficient tumours are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibitors due to synthetic lethality from dual HR and BER impairment.

nodes.label: PARP inhibitors (synthetic lethality)
nodes.description: BRCA1-deficient tumours are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibitors due to synthetic lethality from dual HR and BER impairment.

nodes.label: ULK1, ATG13, FIP200, ATG101
nodes.description: ULK1 functions as part of a stable complex with ATG13, FIP200 (RB1CC1), and ATG101 to initiate autophagosome formation.

nodes.label: ULK1 (at Ser757)
nodes.description: Under nutrient-rich conditions, mTORC1 phosphorylates ULK1 at Ser757, disrupting the ULK1-AMPK interaction and suppressing autophagy.

nodes.label: ULK1
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates ULK1 at multiple lysine residues, promoting its kinase activity and autophagy initiation under glucose starvation.

nodes.label: STRAD and MO25 for activity
nodes.description: Without STRAD and MO25 binding, LKB1 remains in the nucleus and exhibits minimal kinase activity.

nodes.label: Thr172
nodes.description: LKB1 is the primary upstream kinase that phosphorylates AMPK at Thr172 within the activation loop, increasing AMPK activity >100-fold.

nodes.label: LKB1 deficiency

nodes.label: Peutz-Jeghers syndrome
nodes.description: Germline loss-of-function mutations in STK11 cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, characterized by hamartomatous polyps and elevated cancer risk.

nodes.label: Beclin1 BH3 domain
nodes.description: Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL bind the BH3 domain of Beclin1, sequestering it and inhibiting autophagy.

nodes.label: Bcl-2 anti-apoptotic proteins
nodes.description: Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL bind the BH3 domain of Beclin1, sequestering it and inhibiting autophagy.

nodes.label: Four distinct class III PI3K complexes
nodes.description: Beclin1 assembles Complex I (Atg14L), II (UVRAG), III (UVRAG+Rubicon), and IV (Bif-1) to regulate autophagy at different stages.
nodes.norm_label: four distinct class iii pi3k complexes

nodes.label: Tumour suppressor (glutamine metabolism)
nodes.description: SIRT4 inhibits GDH activity, restricting anaplerotic carbon supply to the TCA cycle in cancer cells, suppressing tumour growth.

nodes.label: MTPα (fatty acid oxidation)
nodes.description: SIRT4 suppresses fatty acid oxidation in the liver by inhibiting mitochondrial trifunctional protein α subunit (MTPα).

nodes.label: H3K18ac
nodes.description: SIRT7 possesses NAD+-dependent deacetylase activity with high selectivity for histone H3 at lysine 18 (H3K18ac), a repressive mark.

nodes.label: Replicative lifespan
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT7 extends the replicative lifespan of primary human cells by maintaining rDNA stability and reducing mitochondrial dysfunction.

nodes.label: 1.5 to 3 mg per liter
nodes.description: Typical red wine contains 1.5 to 3 mg/L trans-resveratrol; high-altitude Malbecs or cool-climate Pinot Noirs can reach up to 5.8 mg/L. A standard 5-ounce glass contains ~0.3 mg.

nodes.label: 0.15 to 1.3 mg per 100g
nodes.description: Raw red grapes contain roughly 0.15 to 1.3 mg resveratrol per 100 grams, mostly concentrated in the skins.

nodes.label: Vine Tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata)
nodes.description: Vine tea (Rattan Tea) dry leaves contain 20% to 30% DHM by weight, making 1-1.5g of dry leaves sufficient for a 300mg therapeutic dose.

nodes.label: Cyanidin-3-glucoside
nodes.description: Black elderberries contain roughly 350 to 450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100g fresh berries; 70-85g (~1 cup) reaches the 300mg therapeutic threshold.

nodes.label: 350 to 450 mg per 100g
nodes.description: Black elderberries contain roughly 350 to 450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100g fresh berries; 70-85g (~1 cup) reaches the 300mg therapeutic threshold.

nodes.label: Water
nodes.description: Honokiol is highly lipophilic with extremely poor water solubility. Traditional hot-water tea extraction is inefficient; ethanol tinctures or supercritical CO2 extracts are required for therapeutic dosing.

nodes.label: Dual mechanism (direct + indirect)
nodes.description: Resveratrol activates SIRT1 through direct allosteric binding at the NTD (Glu230) AND indirect activation via the PDE4/cAMP/Epac1/Ca2+/CaMKKβ/AMPK/NAMPT/NAD+ axis.

nodes.label: Tenovin-6
nodes.description: Tenovin-6 inhibits SIRT2 with IC50 = 10 µM, making it the more potent sirtuin target compared to SIRT1.

nodes.label: Tenovins
nodes.description: By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks.

nodes.label: p53 (via hyperacetylation)
nodes.description: By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks.

nodes.label: Xenograft models
nodes.description: Tenovin-1 and Tenovin-6 significantly delay tumor growth in human cancer mouse xenograft models (BL2 and ARN8) at single-digit micromolar concentrations.

nodes.label: Splitomicin
nodes.description: Splitomicin inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 96 µM in vitro, blocking NAD+-dependent deacetylation.

nodes.label: NF-κB p65
nodes.description: Splitomicin treatment reduces intracellular deacetylase activity, resulting in hyperacetylation and enhanced nuclear translocation of NF-κB p65, amplifying inflammatory transcription.

nodes.label: Ischemic preconditioning cardioprotection
nodes.description: In ischemic preconditioning models, splitomicin reverses protective lysine deacetylation and abolishes preconditioning-induced cardioprotection.

nodes.label: Cambinol
nodes.description: Cambinol inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 56 µM, blocking access to both NAD+ and acetyl-lysine substrates.

nodes.label: Cancer cell migration and invasion
nodes.description: In human hepatocellular carcinoma and lung cancer cells, cambinol treatment impairs cell migration and invasion in a dose-dependent manner.

nodes.label: Cancer cells to chemotherapy
nodes.description: Cambinol combination with chemotherapeutic agents dramatically sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy-induced apoptosis.

nodes.label: Salermide
nodes.description: Salermide is a potent synthetic sirtuin inhibitor with improved inhibitory potency against SIRT1 compared to parent compound sirtinol.

nodes.label: Proapoptotic genes (via H4K16ac)
nodes.description: Salermide inhibits SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of H4K16, leading to epigenetic reactivation of proapoptotic genes aberrantly repressed in cancer cells.

nodes.label: Cancer cell lines (MOLT4, MDA-MB-231, RKO)
nodes.description: Salermide induces robust apoptosis in leukemia MOLT4, breast MDA-MB-231, and colon RKO cancer cells.

nodes.label: Colorectal cancer stem cells
nodes.description: Salermide inhibits colorectal carcinoma cancer stem cell self-renewal capacity and reduces tumorigenesis.

nodes.label: Sirtinol
nodes.description: Sirtinol inhibits SIRT1 with IC50 ≈ 131 µM, preventing deacetylation of histones and non-histone target proteins.

nodes.label: Senescence-like growth arrest
nodes.description: Sirtinol treatment induces senescence-like growth arrest in human lung cancer H1299 cells.

nodes.label: Apoptotic and autophagic cell death (MCF-7)
nodes.description: In MCF-7 human breast cancer cells, sirtinol triggers both apoptotic and autophagic programmed cell death.

nodes.label: CD38 inhibitor 78c
nodes.description: 78c is a highly potent, selective, and orally bioactive small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity.

nodes.label: CD38 (NAD+-glycohydrolase)
nodes.description: 78c is a highly potent, selective, and orally bioactive small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity.

nodes.label: NAD+ levels
nodes.description: By selectively inhibiting CD38, 78c prevents age-related degradation of NAD+, keeping cellular pools high.

nodes.label: Sirtuin activity (SIRT1, SIRT3)
nodes.description: 78c indirectly boosts SIRT1 and SIRT3 by maintaining NAD+ co-substrate availability.
Administration of 78c to naturally aged male mice yielded a ~14% lifespan boost.

nodes.label: NMN and NR
nodes.description: 78c enhances the efficacy of exogenous NAD+ precursors NMN and NR by preventing their rapid degradation by CD38.

nodes.label: Fucoidan
nodes.description: Fucoidan-FV activates SIRT6 by increasing SIRT6 protein abundance and enhancing its mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity.

nodes.label: SIRT6 mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity
nodes.description: Unlike most SIRT6 activators that target deacetylase activity, fucoidan preferentially stimulates the ADP-ribosyltransferase function of SIRT6.

nodes.label: LINE-1 expression (HGPS fibroblasts)
nodes.description: Fucoidan-FV (50–100 µg/mL) reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts.

nodes.label: Healthspan and lifespan (aged mice)
nodes.description: SIRT6 activator fucoidan extends healthspan and lifespan in aged wild-type mice.

nodes.label: ML385
nodes.description: ML385 binds directly to the NRF2 bZIP domain, blocking heterodimerization with small Maf proteins and preventing ARE-driven transcription.

nodes.label: AGK2
nodes.description: AGK2 is a highly selective SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 3.5 µM) with over 10-fold selectivity over SIRT1 and SIRT3.

nodes.label: α-synuclein-mediated toxicity
nodes.description: SIRT2 inhibition via AGK2 prevents deacetylation of α-synuclein and microtubule elements, suppressing aggregation and protecting cell viability in Parkinson's disease models.

nodes.label: Ischemic stroke
nodes.description: AGK2 administration confers significant neuroprotection under ischemic and hypoxic conditions by suppressing phospho-JNK and FOXO3a, preventing caspase-3 cleavage.

nodes.label: SIRT6 centenarian variants (N308K/A313S)
nodes.description: Centenarian SIRT6 variants elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through weakened interaction with Vimentin, independent of mRNA levels.

nodes.label: SIRT6 protein levels
nodes.description: Centenarian SIRT6 variants elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through weakened interaction with Vimentin, independent of mRNA levels.

nodes.label: SIRT6 N308K mutation
nodes.description: The N308K substitution selectively reduces SIRT6-vimentin interaction, leading to increased SIRT6 protein levels.

nodes.label: Vimentin

CCL2 (MCP-1) is a SASP chemokine regulated by IL-1α and IL-1β, strong chemoattractant for monocytes.
SAMD refers to the impairment of mitochondrial structure and function that is a hallmark of senescent cells.
SAMD is an active driver of the SASP through ROS elevation and mtDNA release activating cGAS-STING.
Minority MOMP in SAMD releases mtDNA into the cytosol without triggering apoptosis.
Released mtDNA from SAMD activates the cGAS-STING innate-immune sensor driving type I interferon and NF-κB SASP.
Dysfunctional mitochondrial complexes elevate ROS causing further DNA damage and amplifying arrest.
Mitochondrial ROS from SAMD activate NF-κB and stress kinases including p38 MAPK.
Metformin improves mitochondrial function and has senomorphic effects relevant to SAMD.
Resveratrol acts as an antioxidant to quench ROS from dysfunctional mitochondria.
Navitoclax (ABT-263) blocks BCL-2/BCL-XL/BCL-W but is limited by thrombocytopenia.
D+Q improved physical function in an IPF pilot study.
Senolytics are tested for osteoarthritis pain and function in clinical trials.
Senotherapeutic is the umbrella term spanning both senolytics (cell elimination) and senomorphics (SASP suppression).
Senotherapeutic spans both senolytics and senomorphics as complementary strategies.
Senotherapeutics selectively target senescent cells to mitigate aging and age-related disease.
Clearing senescent cells in murine models improves healthspan and restores tissue function.
Senotherapy includes both senolytic and senomorphic approaches to mitigate senescence-driven pathology.
Senotherapy targets the SASP as the primary secretory phenotype driving senescence-associated pathology.
Immunosenescence is the systemic deterioration of immune function that accompanies aging.
Immunosenescence is accompanied by inflammaging, a chronic state of innate immune activation.
Autophagy inducers including rapamycin provide potential to partially reverse systemic immunosenescence.
Metformin is an autophagy inducer with potential to partially reverse immunosenescence.
Spermidine is an autophagy inducer with potential to partially reverse immunosenescence.
Immunosenescence features perturbed memory responses, especially in T cell immunity, with accumulation of memory T cell subsets.
mtDNA released into the cytosol activates cGAS-STING, driving type I interferon and NF-κB SASP.
SADS is the decompaction of constitutive pericentromeric/pericentrosomal satellite heterochromatin in senescent cells.
SADS-generated contacts interact with inflammatory SASP gene loci, altering their chromatin state.
SADS affects constitutive heterochromatin independently of SAHF, which affects facultative heterochromatin.
Satellite-repeat derepression in SADS connects to retrotransposon/LINE-1 and HERV activation.
CD4+ and CD8+ T cells recognize senescent cell antigens and orchestrate the immune response.
Immunosenescence features perturbed memory responses, especially in T cell immunity.
p21 inhibits Cyclin-Dependent Kinase 2 (CDK2) and enforces G1/S arrest.
p21 supports an early secretory phenotype including CXCL14 and IGFBP3, placing stressed cells under immunosurveillance.
Sublethal mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization by BAX/BAK releases mtDNA into the cytosol.
mtDNA released by minority MOMP activates cGAS-STING, driving SASP without full cell death.
SCAPs including BCL-2 family proteins restrain MOMP to keep senescent cells alive despite mitochondrial stress.
Reduced Lamin B1 detaches lamina-associated domains from the nuclear periphery in senescent cells.
Activin A is a homodimer of inhibin beta-A (INHBA) subunits and a member of the TGFβ superfamily.
Activin A signals through the type I receptor ALK4 and type II receptor activin RIIA/RIIB, phosphorylating SMAD2 and SMAD3.
Phosphorylated SMAD2/3 complex with SMAD4 and translocate to the nucleus to regulate target gene transcription.
Activin A-SMAD signaling induces p15^INK4b and p21^CIP1 in receiving cells during paracrine senescence.
Activin A-SMAD signaling induces p21^CIP1 in receiving cells.
Activin A is a TGF-β family ligand component of the SASP mediating paracrine senescence.
Activin A contributes to paracrine senescence alongside TGF-β1, BMP2, and GDF15; blocking antibodies partially rescue paracrine arrest.
Activin A was identified as a TGF-β family ligand acutely upregulated during OIS (Acosta et al., 2013).
Activin A expression is driven by IL-1α and NF-κB during senescence.
Follistatin binds and neutralizes activin A extracellularly.
CDKN2B encodes p15INK4b, a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor that blocks CDK4/6.
CDKN2B is a direct transcriptional target of TGFβ signaling via SMAD3/SMAD4 complexes binding SMAD-binding elements.
p15INK4b is a key effector of TGF-β-mediated paracrine senescence; its induction is essential for paracrine growth arrest.
CDKN2B is frequently silenced by promoter methylation in leukaemias, lymphomas, and gliomas.
The ASAP→SASP transition is gated through DDR kinases (ATM), TAK1, and downstream p38 MAPK/PI3K/Akt/mTOR engagement.
ATM is phosphorylated and translocated from nucleus to cytoplasm in the ASAP, acting as upstream DDR gate.
Apigenin blocks the transition of the ASAP toward the SASP by disrupting ATM-HSPA8 and HSPA8-p38 MAPK crosstalk.
The PRDX6→HSPA8 axis controls the ASAP→SASP transition; apigenin binds PRDX6 inhibiting its iPLA2 activity.
HSPA8 activation and its interactions with ATM and p38 MAPK mediate ASAP maturation into the SASP.
The ATM-TRAF6-TAK1 axis drives ASAP signaling; TAK1 activates p38 MAPK and NF-κB downstream.
CCL20 (MIP-3α) is a CC chemokine that signals exclusively through the receptor CCR6.
CCL20 is the sole ligand for CCR6, a Gαi-coupled GPCR driving chemotaxis via PI3K/Akt, p38 MAPK, and Ca2+ flux.
CCL20 is a SASP chemokine that contributes to paracrine growth arrest in neighbouring cells.
CCL20 is among SASP components that autocrinally reinforce senescence and induce paracrine arrest in receiving cells.
CCL20 expression is driven by NF-κB and induced by IL-1α, IL-1β, and TNF-α.
The CCL20-CCR6 axis links the SASP to adaptive immunity by recruiting TH17 cells.
CCL20-mediated immune recruitment can contribute to chronic inflammation and age-related tissue dysfunction.
p15INK4b specifically binds and inhibits CDK4 and CDK6, preventing cyclin D-CDK complex formation.
p15INK4b maintains Rb in its hypophosphorylated growth-suppressive state, enforcing G1 cell cycle arrest.
p15INK4b cooperates with p21CIP1 to enforce G1 arrest during paracrine senescence.
HLA-E is a non-classical (class Ib) major histocompatibility complex molecule with limited polymorphism.
HLA-E is the ligand for the inhibitory receptor NKG2A/CD94 heterodimer on NK cells and CD8+ T cells.
HLA-E-NKG2A/CD94 engagement delivers an inhibitory signal that blunts NK cell cytotoxic killing.
HLA-E-NKG2A/CD94 engagement on CD8+ T cells suppresses cytotoxic killing.
SASP cytokines IL-6 and IL-8 upregulate HLA-E, engaging NKG2A/CD94 to suppress NK- and CD8+ T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity.
HLA-E upregulation allows senescent cells to persist and tumor cells to escape clearance.
By dampening immune surveillance, HLA-E upregulation allows senescent cells to persist.
Inflammasomes are cytosolic supramolecular complexes of the innate immune system.
Canonical inflammasomes activate Caspase-1 which processes pro-IL-1β, pro-IL-18, and GSDMD.
Caspase-1 processes pro-IL-1β into mature IL-1β for secretion.
Caspase-1/4/5/11 cleave GSDMD; the N-terminal fragment oligomerizes forming pores that cause pyroptosis.
Chronic inflammasome activation by sterile stimuli drives persistent inflammation and age-related diseases.
Senescent cells accumulate DAMPs (HMGB1, mtDNA, oxidized lipids) that activate NLRP3 in neighbouring macrophages.
Caspase-1 or IL-1R inhibitors blunt SASP expression, placing canonical inflammasome activation upstream of the SASP during OIS.
The noncanonical inflammasome is an innate immune surveillance pathway distinct from the canonical NLRP3/caspase-1 pathway.
Caspase-5 (human) is the inducible noncanonical effector caspase that cleaves IL-1α and GSDMD.
Caspase-11 (mouse) is the noncanonical effector caspase that cleaves IL-1α and GSDMD.
Noncanonical inflammasome-mediated IL-1α cleavage is the critical upstream trigger for SASP in senescent cells.
cGAS-STING controls CASP5 expression upstream; cGAS knockdown reduces CASP5 expression.
GSDMD pore formation triggers K+ efflux, activating the canonical NLRP3/caspase-1 inflammasome downstream.
Hexa-acylated lipid A of LPS binds directly to the CARD domain of caspase-4/5/11 inducing dimerization and activation.
MyD88 is a cytoplasmic adaptor protein serving as the central hub of TLR and IL-1R signaling.
IL-1R recruits MyD88 via TIR-TIR interactions; MyD88 assembles the myddosome signaling complex.
MyD88 recruits IRAK4 via DD-DD interactions, followed by IRAK1/IRAK2 recruitment in a 6:4:4 stoichiometry.
Active IRAK4 phosphorylates IRAK1; IRAK1 recruits TRAF6 through its C-terminal TRAF6-binding motifs.
MyD88 assembles into the helical oligomeric myddosome with IRAK4 and IRAK1/2 as the scaffolding platform.
Senescent cell surface IL-1α engages IL-1R on macrophages, recruiting MyD88 to activate NF-κB and SASP amplification.
MyD88-dependent IL-1R signaling is required for SASP establishment and maintenance; IRAK1 depletion suppresses SASP.
Persistent MyD88-dependent IL-1R signaling drives age-related chronic inflammation.
MDSCs are a heterogeneous population of immature myeloid cells with potent immunosuppressive activity.
MDSCs deplete L-arginine via arginase-1, produce ROS and peroxynitrite that impair T-cell receptor signalling.
SASP factor GM-CSF stimulates myeloid expansion and biases differentiation toward immunosuppressive MDSCs.
CCL2 recruits CCR2+ myeloid precursors into senescent/tumour tissue.
IL-6 and other pro-inflammatory SASP cytokines promote MDSC accumulation and activation via JAK/STAT3 signalling.
MDSCs impair immune-mediated clearance of senescent cells, allowing senescent-cell accumulation.
Elevated MDSC frequencies rise with age as part of immunosenescence.
Chronic SASP-driven MDSC expansion contributes to age-related inflammation.
GM-CSF and CCL2 skew myeloid differentiation toward immunosuppressive MDSCs and specific macrophage phenotypes.
Caspase-5 cleaves pro-IL-1α at a conserved site distinct from the calpain cleavage site, essential for SASP establishment.
Active caspase-4/5/11 cleave gasdermin D between its N-terminal pore-forming domain and C-terminal inhibitory domain.
Paracrine reprogramming alters differentiation status (stemness, EMT) while paracrine senescence induces growth arrest.
Chronic SASP (IL-6, IL-8 via JAK/STAT3) promotes cancer stem-cell traits and stemness in neighbouring epithelial/tumour cells.
VEGF-C is a member of the VEGF family of cysteine-knot growth factors.
VEGF-C signals primarily through VEGFR-3 on lymphatic endothelium.
At higher concentrations or after proteolytic processing, VEGF-C also engages VEGFR2 on blood vascular endothelium.
VEGF-C is a secreted SASP growth factor, induced during RAS-driven OIS as early as 2-3 days after RAS activation.
VEGFR2/FLT3 inhibitor suppressed paracrine senescence; VEGF family signaling is a branch mediating paracrine arrest.
VEGF-C expression is induced downstream of RAS/RAF/MEK oncogenic signalling and reinforced by IL-1α and NF-κB.
Processed VEGF-C engages VEGFR2 to support blood-vessel angiogenesis.
Full-length VEGF-C preferentially activates VEGFR-3 and promotes lymphatic vessel sprouting.
Stalled/dysfunctional replication forks generate single-strand DNA gaps that engage ATR-CHK1 cascade.
DNA replication stress activates ATM-CHK2 cascade converging on p53 stabilization.
The CDKN2A locus encoding p16^INK4a is derepressed in OIS via loss of PRC1/2-mediated H3K27me3.
OIS cells transmit senescence to neighbouring normal cells via secreted SASP factors (Acosta et al., 2013).
OIS bypass through loss of p53, p16INK4A, or PTEN is a prerequisite for progression to malignancy.
OIS cells are susceptible to senolytic drugs like Navitoclax (Bcl-2/Bcl-xL inhibitor).
SIR2 from S. cerevisiae is the founding member of the sirtuin family; mammalian homologues are SIRT1–7.
Hydrolysis of one NAD+ molecule produced one molecule of nicotinamide, and one of OAADPr.
OAADPr binds to and activates the cytoplasmic domain of the TRPM2 non-selective cation channel.
Lifespan extension by CR is not seen if cells lack the SIR2 gene.
On medium with 0.5% glucose vs standard 2% glucose, replicative lifespan was ~30% longer.
Lifespan extension by dietary restriction also requires the Sir2 gene in Drosophila.
Higher levels of SIRT1 in CR rodents may be one of the reasons for their decreased inflammatory responses.
CR increases SIRT1 and NAD+/nicotinamide ratios in the brain.
Pancreatic islets of mice under a CR diet show effects suggesting SIRT4 is downregulated by CR.
CR prevents genetically engineered mice prone to Alzheimer's disease from developing β-amyloid neuropathology.
Integration of an extra copy of the SIR2 gene increased the replicative lifespan up to 30%.
C. elegans carrying a chromosome duplication containing sir-2.1 exhibits up to a 50% lifespan increase.
Lifespan extension is strictly dependent on the forkhead transcriptional factor DAF-16.
An extra copy of the Sir2 gene expressed ubiquitously causes females to live longer by 29%.
SIRT1-dependent deacetylation of p53 inhibits its transactivation activity and suppresses apoptosis in response to oxidative stress and DNA damage.
HIC1 forms a complex with SIRT1 via its N-terminal POZ domain, which binds directly to the SIRT1 promoter and represses its expression.
Deacetylated Ku70 complexes with the proapoptotic factor Bax, sequestering it away from mitochondria.
E2F1 binds directly to the SIRT1 promoter and induces its transcription.
Deacetylation inhibits the transactivation potential of RelA/p65, reducing inflammation.
The expression of this sirtuin increases dramatically during mitosis and is hyperphosphorylated during the G2/M phase transition.
SIRT6 knockout mice displayed signs of premature aging, such as decreased size, loss of subcutaneous fat, lymphocyte apoptosis, colitis, abnormal spine curvature.
Activation of Tat increases viral transcription.
When SIRT1 is overexpressed in pancreatic β-cells, mice exhibit enhanced glucose-stimulated insulin secretion and ATP production.
SIRT4 regulates amino-acid-stimulated insulin secretion in pancreatic β-cells.
Animals displayed increased mitochondria concomitant with increased SIRT1 and PGC1-α activity.
A variant of the SIRT3 gene, specifically in an enhancer within intron 5, correlates with male lifespan beyond 90 years.
Three single nucleotide polymorphisms in the SIRT1 gene of Finnish human subjects were significantly associated with systemic energy expenditure.
SIRT1 knockout mice are markedly smaller than littermates, develop slowly, show eye morphogenesis and cardiac septation perturbations.
Both males and females that survive to adulthood are sterile; males have low sperm counts and females fail to ovulate.
Nmnat is primarily responsible for protection from axonal degeneration; protection is due primarily to the actions of SIRT1.
Protects glomerular mesangial cells from TGF-β dependent apoptosis.
May help protect against heart failure by promoting degradation of H2A.Z, a factor known to promote cardiac hypertrophy.
p33ING1b interacts with human SIRT1, thereby inhibiting its ability to deacetylate p53, which negatively regulates transcription of AFP.
Administration of adiponectin to high-fat-fed obese mice improves insulin sensitivity while lowering blood glucose.
PGC-1α null-mice are considerably more sensitive to neuronal loss by MPTP and kainic acid.

Inhibiting PDE4 prevents cAMP degradation, leading to cAMP accumulation and downstream AMPK activation.
High cAMP activates Epac1 (Exchange Protein directly Activated by cAMP), which triggers Ca2+ release from the ER.
Epac1 activation causes release of calcium from the endoplasmic reticulum into the cytoplasm.
Cytoplasmic Ca2+ activates CaMKKβ (calmodulin-dependent protein kinase kinase beta), which phosphorylates and activates AMPK.
Activated AMPK increases the expression of NAMPT, the rate-limiting enzyme in the NAD+ salvage pathway.
NAMPT condenses nicotinamide with PRPP to form NMN, the rate-limiting step in the NAD+ salvage pathway.
NAMPT is the rate-limiting enzyme in the NAD+ salvage pathway; its upregulation boosts cellular NAD+ levels, fueling SIRT1.
Deacetylated PGC-1α migrates to the nucleus to drive mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative phosphorylation genes.
SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a, shifting transcription toward stress-resistance genes (SOD2, Catalase) and autophagy, away from apoptosis.
SIRT1 deacetylates the NF-κB subunit, preventing it from binding DNA and downregulating pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6).
Deacetylated FOXO3a upregulates endogenous antioxidant enzymes including SOD2 and Catalase.
Deacetylation inhibits NF-κB transcriptional activity, reducing expression of TNF-α, IL-1β, and IL-6.
Endothelial SIRT1 activation by resveratrol increases eNOS expression and activity, promoting nitric oxide production and vasodilation.
Via AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α pathway, resveratrol reduces hepatic steatosis in animal models of diet-induced obesity.
Honokiol physically interacts with SIRT3, increasing its deacetylase activity and upregulating SIRT3 protein expression.

Honokiol is highly lipophilic with extremely poor water solubility. Traditional hot-water tea extraction is inefficient; ethanol tinctures or supercritical CO2 extracts are required for therapeutic dosing.
Honokiol-activated SIRT3 deacetylates MnSOD at K68 and K122, dramatically increasing its ROS-scavenging activity.
SIRT3 deacetylates OSCP, a subunit of the mitochondrial F1Fo-ATPase, optimizing ATP synthase coupling and boosting energy output.
Honokiol-mediated SIRT3 activation reverses cardiac hypertrophy and protects from doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in preclinical models.
In kidneys, Honokiol suppresses NF-κB/TGF-β1 pathway via SIRT3, limiting renal tubulointerstitial fibrosis.
Dihydromyricetin (DHM) activates SIRT3 mitochondrial deacetylase activity, leading to MnSOD deacetylation and ROS reduction.
DHM activates AMPK, which synergistically increases NAD+ levels via NAMPT upregulation, further potentiating SIRT3.
Vine tea (Rattan Tea) dry leaves contain 20% to 30% DHM by weight, making 1-1.5g of dry leaves sufficient for a 300mg therapeutic dose.
UBCS039 is a pyrrolo[1,2-a]quinoxaline reported as the first synthetic activator of SIRT6 deacetylase activity (EC50 = 38 μM).
MDL-801 is a highly potent, cell-permeable synthetic allosteric activator of SIRT6 binding the hydrophobic pocket.
Cyanidin, a natural anthocyanidin found in red berries, increases SIRT6 activity by over 50-fold in certain in vitro assays.
SIRT6 activation results in rapid deacetylation of H3K9ac and H3K56ac on chromatin, promoting chromatin compaction and DNA repair.
By suppressing glycolysis and driving tumor cells toward autophagy, SIRT6 activators like UBCS039 demonstrate tumor-suppressive activity.
Direct activation of SIRT2 is rarely sought because overactivity is associated with neurotoxicity in neurodegeneration contexts.
SIRT2 inhibitors are investigated for neurodegenerative diseases where blocking SIRT2 rescues microtubule stability and protects neurons from aggregation toxicity.
NMN and NR serve as universal indirect pan-sirtuin activators by raising cellular NAD+ levels, the obligate co-substrate for all sirtuins.

microRNAs (miRNAs) can negatively regulate inflammation by repressing SIRT1. Downregulation of miRNAs such as miR-217 and miR-543 mitigated the inflammatory response.
Downregulation of miRNAs such as miR-217 and miR-543 mitigated the inflammatory response by regulating the SIRT1/AMPK/NF-κB signaling pathway.
miR-378 reduced SIRT1 activity and facilitated the inflammatory pathway involving NF-κB-TNFα by targeting 5'-AMPK subunit gamma-2.
the RNase monocyte chemoattractant protein-induced protein 1 alleviated inflammatory responses by promoting the expression of SIRT1 mediated via miR-9.

the SIRT6 activator MDL-800 mitigated UUO-induced kidney tubulointerstitial inflammation and fibrosis.
EX-527, also called Selisistat, is the first known selective (over SIRT2/3) and cell-permeable SIRT1 (IC50 = 0.098 μM) inhibitor.
SirReal2 is a potent SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 0.14 μM) with minimal effects on SIRT1 and SIRT3.
Suramin, a polyanionic urea derivative, was potent SIRT inhibitor with an IC50 of 297 nM, 1150 nM, and 22 μM for SIRT1, SIRT2, and SIRT5, respectively.
SIRT1 knockout in dendritic cells (DCs) restrained the generation of regulatory T cells.
SIRT1 knockout in dendritic cells (DCs) drove T helper 1 cell development, promoting inflammation.
SIRT6 deficiency in macrophages resulted in inflammation with increases in acetylation and greater stability of FoxO1.
SIRT6 in pancreatic β cells deacetylates FoxO1 to maintain glucose-sensing ability and systemic glucose tolerance.
SIRT6 deacetylated FoxO1 and subsequently increased the expression of glucose-dependent transporter 2 (GLUT2).
SIRT5-induced deacetylation of lactate dehydrogenase B (LDHB) triggers hyperactivation of autophagy; a key event in tumorigenesis.
Nuclear SIRT1 enhanced by resveratrol was found to induce superoxide dismutase, an antioxidant enzyme which suppressed cell death in cardiomyocytes.
In SIRT3 deficient mouse models, signs of severe cardiac hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis were present when a hypertrophic stimulus was given.
Transgenic mouse models engineered for over-expression of SIRT3 were significantly less amenable to stimuli-induced hypertrophy.
SIRT7 deficient mice had myocardium defined by extensive fibrosis and high basal rates of apoptosis, resulting in high levels of cardiomyopathy.
Only when Resveratrol is ingested in the red wine matrix does it possess the bioavailability to achieve efficacious levels.
Quercetin and Ethanol are compounds identified in red wine, which are perhaps necessary to amend the activity of catabolic enzymes, thus augmenting Resveratrol activity.
The French Paradox reflects the reduced incidence of Cardiovascular Disease found in some French populations with moderate wine consumption despite a high-fat intake.
In vascular smooth muscle, in vivo studies reveal Resveratrol's ability to propagate SIRT1 expression resulted in decreased angiotensin II-induced hypertension.
TGF-beta1 binds TβRII, which recruits and phosphorylates TβRI, leading to SMAD2/3 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation.
TGF-beta1 activates SMAD3-dependent transcription of pro-fibrotic genes (COL1A1, COL3A1, FN1, ACTA2, TIMP1) across multiple organs.
Hyperactivated SMAD3 binds the 3'-UTR of the TFEB gene and inhibits its transcription, reducing lysosomal biogenesis and autophagic flux.
BRCA1 is recruited to DSBs by the MRN complex, promotes end resection, and facilitates RAD51 loading via PALB2/BRCA2.
Loss of BRCA1 leads to increased autophagy as a compensatory survival mechanism in breast and ovarian cancers.
BRCA1-deficient tumours are exquisitely sensitive to PARP inhibitors due to synthetic lethality from dual HR and BER impairment.
Germline loss-of-function mutations in STK11 cause Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, characterized by hamartomatous polyps and elevated cancer risk.
Bcl-2 and Bcl-xL bind the BH3 domain of Beclin1, sequestering it and inhibiting autophagy.
Black elderberries contain roughly 350 to 450 mg cyanidin-3-glucoside per 100g fresh berries; 70-85g (~1 cup) reaches the 300mg therapeutic threshold.
Tenovin-6 inhibits SIRT2 with IC50 = 10 µM, making it the more potent sirtuin target compared to SIRT1.
Tenovin-6 shows moderate inhibitory activity against SIRT3 with IC50 = 67 µM.
By inhibiting SIRT1/SIRT2-mediated deacetylation, Tenovins promote p53 hyperacetylation and reactivation of p53-dependent transcriptional networks.
Tenovin-1 and Tenovin-6 significantly delay tumor growth in human cancer mouse xenograft models (BL2 and ARN8) at single-digit micromolar concentrations.
Splitomicin inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 96 µM in vitro, blocking NAD+-dependent deacetylation.
Splitomicin inhibits human SIRT2 with IC50 = 113 µM in vitro.
Splitomicin treatment reduces intracellular deacetylase activity, resulting in hyperacetylation and enhanced nuclear translocation of NF-κB p65, amplifying inflammatory transcription.
In ischemic preconditioning models, splitomicin reverses protective lysine deacetylation and abolishes preconditioning-induced cardioprotection.
Cambinol inhibits human SIRT1 with IC50 = 56 µM, blocking access to both NAD+ and acetyl-lysine substrates.
Cambinol inhibits human SIRT2 with IC50 = 59 µM with minimal activity against SIRT3 or other class I/II HDACs.
In human hepatocellular carcinoma and lung cancer cells, cambinol treatment impairs cell migration and invasion in a dose-dependent manner.
Cambinol combination with chemotherapeutic agents dramatically sensitizes cancer cells to chemotherapy-induced apoptosis.
Salermide is a potent synthetic sirtuin inhibitor with improved inhibitory potency against SIRT1 compared to parent compound sirtinol.
Salermide possesses significantly improved inhibitory potency against SIRT2 compared to sirtinol.
Salermide inhibits SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of H4K16, leading to epigenetic reactivation of proapoptotic genes aberrantly repressed in cancer cells.
Salermide induces robust apoptosis in leukemia MOLT4, breast MDA-MB-231, and colon RKO cancer cells.
Salermide inhibits colorectal carcinoma cancer stem cell self-renewal capacity and reduces tumorigenesis.
Sirtinol inhibits SIRT1 with IC50 ≈ 131 µM, preventing deacetylation of histones and non-histone target proteins.
Sirtinol inhibits SIRT2 with IC50 ≈ 38–68 µM in various assays.
Sirtinol treatment induces senescence-like growth arrest in human lung cancer H1299 cells.
In MCF-7 human breast cancer cells, sirtinol triggers both apoptotic and autophagic programmed cell death.
78c is a highly potent, selective, and orally bioactive small-molecule inhibitor of CD38 NAD+-glycohydrolase activity.
By selectively inhibiting CD38, 78c prevents age-related degradation of NAD+, keeping cellular pools high.
78c indirectly boosts SIRT1 and SIRT3 by maintaining NAD+ co-substrate availability.

Fucoidan-FV activates SIRT6 by increasing SIRT6 protein abundance and enhancing its mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity.
Unlike most SIRT6 activators that target deacetylase activity, fucoidan preferentially stimulates the ADP-ribosyltransferase function of SIRT6.
Fucoidan-FV (50–100 µg/mL) reduces LINE-1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts.
SIRT6 activator fucoidan extends healthspan and lifespan in aged wild-type mice.
ML385 binds directly to the NRF2 bZIP domain, blocking heterodimerization with small Maf proteins and preventing ARE-driven transcription.
AGK2 is a highly selective SIRT2 inhibitor (IC50 = 3.5 µM) with over 10-fold selectivity over SIRT1 and SIRT3.

AGK2 administration confers significant neuroprotection under ischemic and hypoxic conditions by suppressing phospho-JNK and FOXO3a, preventing caspase-3 cleavage.
Centenarian SIRT6 variants elevate endogenous SIRT6 protein through weakened interaction with Vimentin, independent of mRNA levels.
The N308K substitution selectively reduces SIRT6-vimentin interaction, leading to increased SIRT6 protein levels.
Vimentin interaction with SIRT6 promotes its degradation; weakened interaction in centenarian variants elevates SIRT6 levels.
CentSIRT6 exhibits enhanced mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity; A313S primarily enhances this activity.
Despite higher SIRT6 protein, CENT hMSCs show increased histone acetylation at H3K9, H3K18, and H3K27, confirming reduced deacetylase activity.
At late passages, CENT hMSCs exhibit higher Ki67-positive cells and fewer SA-β-gal-positive cells, demonstrating delayed senescence.
Centenarian variants ameliorate multiple aging phenotypes in progerin-expressing hMSCs: higher Ki67, reduced SA-β-gal, decreased p16/p21, reduced IL-6, increased Lamin B1.
CENT hMSCs show better-maintained suppression of LINE-1 elements under progerin-induced stress, with reduced ORF1p and ORF2p proteins.
AAV-mediated delivery of CentSIRT6 reduced LINE1 ORF1p and ORF2p protein levels in HGPS patient-derived fibroblasts.
SIRT6 mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1 recruits HP1α to package LINE-1 into heterochromatin.
The phosphatase CDC14B dephosphorylates SIRT2, triggering its ubiquitination and degradation by the 26S proteasome, promoting exit from mitosis.
The ICE Mouse uses inducible I-PpoI expression to trigger targeted DSBs that are repaired without introducing mutations.
Induction of DSBs followed by repair produces accelerated epigenetic aging and physiological decline, supporting the RCM hypothesis.
The induced changes in the ICE Mouse shift the epigenetic clock, consistent with relocalization of chromatin modifiers.
Because no mutations are introduced, the phenotype is attributed to loss of epigenetic information rather than hardware damage, supporting the Information Theory of Aging.
I-PpoI recognizes and cleaves a specific 15–20 bp sequence within rRNA gene repeats, generating double-strand breaks.
Sinclair identified SIRT1 as a mediator of caloric restriction benefits and discovered resveratrol as a STAC in a landmark 2003 study.
In 2003, Sinclair showed resveratrol extends yeast lifespan via Sir2 and later demonstrated parallel effects in higher organisms.
Sinclair co-founded Sirtris Pharmaceuticals (acquired by GlaxoSmithKline) to develop STACs as therapeutics, including SRT1720 and SRT2104.
The Sinclair lab developed the ICE Mouse to test the RCM hypothesis using mutation-free DSBs.
Sinclair proposed the information-theory-of-aging framework, positing that aging results from loss of epigenetic information rather than damage accumulation.
SIRT1 directly regulates BDNF transcription by deacetylating and repressing Hes1 (a transcriptional repressor of BDNF), relieving inhibition and promoting neuronal survival.
SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, which co-activates the BDNF promoter, linking mitochondrial biogenesis to neurotrophic support.
Exercise raises both BDNF and NAD+ levels, and SIRT1 may mediate exercise-induced BDNF upregulation in the hippocampus.
Positive histone acetyltransferases PCAF and GCN5 acetylate MyoD, enhancing its DNA-binding capacity and recruitment of transcriptional machinery.
Upon oncogenic stress, the PML-IV isoform recruits both p53 and SIRT1 into PML nuclear bodies.
PML-IV overexpression is sufficient to induce senescence in a p53-dependent manner; loss of PML accelerates tumorigenesis.
The Mediterranean Diet's resveratrol content activates SIRT1, linking the diet to longevity pathways.
The PREDIMED trial demonstrated that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with olive oil or nuts significantly reduced major cardiovascular events.
